tekst:
The Dallas Mavericks have agreed on a two-way NBA deal with former first-round pick Walter Clayton Jr., sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Wednesday.
Clayton was waived earlier this week by the Memphis Grizzlies ahead of the league's roster cut-down deadline. He is joining the Mavericks after clearing waivers.
Memphis acquired Clayton from Utah on Feb. 3 in the eight-player trade that sent Jaren Jackson Jr., Jock Landale, John Konchar and Vince Williams Jr. to the Jazz. Clayton played 24 games for the Grizzlies last season after the trade, averaging 9.7 points, 2.1 rebounds and 5.7 assists and shooting 36.6% from 3-point range.
Clayton, 23, was the No. 18 pick in the 2025 draft after helping Florida win its third national title. He was named the Final Four's Most Outstanding Player and was a consensus first-team All-American in 2025.
The Mavericks, still light on ball handlers despite the return of Kyrie Irving from his ACL injury, could use the depth Clayton provides in their backcourt.

vistina: NBA Player Movement 2026-10-19: Dallas Mavericks waived forward Dwight Powell.
tekst:
By Eurohoops team / info@eurohoops.net
The Dallas Mavericks are waiving veteran center Dwight Powell, ESPN’s Shams Charania reported, ending his 12-year stint with the franchise.
The 35-year-old was on a non-guaranteed contract as Dallas finalized its roster ahead of the regular season. His departure closes a chapter spanning the Mavericks’ eras with Dirk Nowitzki, Luka Doncic and Cooper Flagg.
Head coach Dusty May had praised Powell’s contribution during preseason, highlighting his leadership and the team’s effectiveness with him on the floor. However, May stressed that roster decisions rested with president Masai Ujiri and general manager Mike Schmitz.
Powell appeared in both preseason games against Houston during the NBA China Games, averaging two points and three rebounds. Beyond those numbers, his physicality and screen setting had continued to earn praise as Dallas weighed its final roster decisions.

vistina: NBA Player Movement 2026-10-19: Los Angeles Lakers waived forward Dalton Knecht.
tekst:
By Eurohoops team / info@eurohoops.net
The Los Angeles Lakers waived Dalton Knecht ahead of the NBA’s roster deadline, while the Milwaukee Bucks also released Kevin Porter Jr. to finalize their squad for the upcoming season.
Knecht’s departure, reported by ESPN’s Shams Charania, ended his two-season stint with the Lakers. The No. 17 pick in the 2024 draft averaged 9.1 points and 2.8 rebounds as a rookie but struggled in his second season. Los Angeles reportedly explored a trade before opting to waive him.
The Lakers had previously agreed to send Knecht to Charlotte in the 2025 trade for Mark Williams, but the deal was rescinded after Williams failed his physical.
Porter, who played for PAOK in 2024 before returning to the NBA, was released as Milwaukee reduced its perimeter options. Injuries limited him to 38 appearances last season, though he averaged 17.4 points, 5.2 rebounds, 7.4 assists and 2.2 steals.
The former PAOK guard joined the Bucks from the Los Angeles Clippers in February 2025. He underwent right knee surgery in April 2026, ending his regular season early.

vistina: NBA Player Movement 2026-10-17: Dallas Mavericks waived guard John Poulakidas.
tekst:
By Stefan Acevski / info@eurohoops.net
The Dallas Mavericks waived John Poulakidas (23 years old, 1.98m) just a few days before the start of the NBA regular season.
During the preseason, where he played under a two-way contract, the 23-year-old guard, who has attracted interest from both Olympiacos and Panathinaikos, averaged 7 points and 1.3 rebounds in 14 minutes per game, with a three-point shooting percentage of 45.5% (80% on free throws and 50% on field goals).
His standout performance during the preseason was against the Pelicans, where he scored 16 points.
Last season, he made his NBA debut with the Mavericks, and during the preseason, he attempted to secure a new contract, but this was not achieved. Now, as a free agent, he is in search of a new team.
Poulakidis has been on the radar of Greek teams, mainly Olympiacos, due to his Greek heritage.
However, he does not yet have a Greek passport, and for this season he will not be able to play as a local player in the Greek league. There’s no such restriction for the EuroLeague.

vistina: NBA Player Movement 2026-10-15: Dallas Mavericks waived forward Jorge Diaz-Graham.
tekst:
By Johnny Askounis/ info@eurohoops.net
The Dallas Mavericks made a quick roster shuffle on Thursday, waiving forward Jorge Diaz Graham only to sign his identical twin brother, Guillermo, about five hours later.
This fast move was mostly a formal roster trick rather than a true split. They simply swapped one brother for the other, and Guillermo will likely be let go soon too. Both twins are on track to play together for the Texas Legends, the G League affiliate of the Mavs, where they are expected to spend the upcoming 2026–27 season.
The Spanish twins first teamed up for Dallas during the Summer League. Before that, they spent three years playing together in the NCAA at Pittsburgh before separating for their final season, when Jorge went to Oregon State and Guillermo went to San Francisco. Their paths crossed again in the G League International Draft, where the Legends picked Jorge first overall and Guillermo third.
In his recent brief run with the main Mavericks team, Jorge put up five points and three rebounds in 12 minutes during Wednesday’s game against New Orleans before being waived to clear a spot for Guillermo.
These moves added to a very international roster. The Mavericks currently have more European players than any other team in the league. Greek John Poulakidas, Spanish Sergio de Larrea, British Tobi Lawal, Spanish Santi Aldama, Turkish Tarik Biberovic, and French Zaccharie Risacher.
As the front office finalizes the regular-season lineup, the team coached by Dusty May is getting ready to host the Atlanta Hawks on Friday to finish the exhibition slate. After that, they start the Regular Season next Wednesday on the road against the Houston Rockets.

vistina: NBA Player Movement 2026-09-25: Dallas Mavericks re-signed forward Dwight Powell to a Contract.
tekst:
By Johnny Askounis/ info@eurohoops.net
The Dallas Mavericks face an immediate roster crunch after re-signing veteran center Dwight Powell on Friday.
This numbers game leaves Tarik Biberovic fighting for his spot just days after his official NBA arrival at the preseason media day.
Dallas carries a full 15-player roster on standard contracts. To fit Powell under the league limit, management must subtract a player through a trade or a waiver. As detailed by Marc Stein of The Stein Line on Sunday, the situation presents a painful dilemma for the front office.
The Turkish forward recently shared his excitement about bringing his ‘lights-out’ perimeter shooting to Texas after an eight-year run with EuroLeague powerhouse Fenerbahce. Dallas genuinely wants to keep him. However, his two-year, $6 million contract includes a flexible second-year team option. This structure, alongside the salaries of Marcus Sasser and Moussa Cisse, makes them the easiest candidates to clear space. The final decision must be announced before the start of the 2026–27 Regular Season on October 19.
To avoid losing the 25-year-old sharpshooter for nothing, they can pursue a trade to reduce the roster size. However, the most likely scenario is to simply waive 35-year-old Powell. Waiving Biberovic or another player instead remains an absolute last resort.

vistina: NBA Player Movement 2026-09-18: Denver Nuggets signed forward Cam Whitmore to a Two-Way Contract.
tekst:
By Johnny Askounis/ info@eurohoops.net
The Denver Nuggets have officially signed forward Cam Whitmore to a two-way contract, the team announced on Friday, ending recent rumors. The move highlights Denver’s current salary cap limitations, as the front office must get creative to add depth around Serbian superstar Nikola Jokic. Despite interest from the Los Angeles Lakers, the 22-year-old forward ultimately chose Colorado as his next landing spot and is already in town participating in workouts.
Whitmore is looking for a fresh start after a challenging stretch with the Washington Wizards. His 2025–26 campaign was cut short in December due to deep vein thrombosis in his right shoulder. When healthy, the former Villanova standout has shown immense promise. Since entering the league as the 20th overall pick in 2020, he has averaged 10.5 points and 3.3 rebounds over 119 career appearances split between Houston and Washington.
For the management, this signing is an ideal low-risk, high-reward move. It allows them to inject explosive young talent into the rotation without taking a hit on the salary cap or triggering luxury tax penalties. Furthermore, because it is a two-way designation, Denver retains exclusive control over his rights, preventing other franchises from poaching him off the roster.
However, the contract structure does come with strict operational boundaries. Whitmore can only be active for a maximum of 50 regular-season games with the team coached by David Adelman, spending the rest of his time developing with their G League affiliate. Additionally, he will be ineligible to suit up for the Playoffs unless Denver decides to convert his deal into a standard 15-man roster spot before the Regular Season comes to a close.

vistina: NBA Player Movement 2026-09-14: LA Clippers received guard Gradey Dick from Toronto Raptors.
tekst:
By Johnny Askounis/ info@eurohoops.net
The Toronto Raptors have finalized a blockbuster trade, securing the return of two-time NBA Finals Most Valuable Player Kawhi Leonard.
Their deal with the Los Angeles Clippers was officially confirmed on Monday. Moving in the opposite direction are Brandon Ingram and Gradey Dick, alongside a hefty package of draft capital consisting of two future first-round picks, a pick swap in 2027, and two future second-round selections.
The completion of the agreement was heavily delayed following its initial handshake on June 30. The NBA previously placed a hold on the transaction to launch an extensive salary-cap circumvention investigation regarding an alleged off-the-books endorsement deal under the Clippers’ roof. After months of regulatory standstill and final disciplinary rulings handed down to the Los Angeles organization, the pathway cleared for the paperwork to be formally processed.
Steering the franchise forward, Raptors general manager and executive vice-president Bobby Webster expressed tremendous enthusiasm about welcoming Leonard back to Canada.
“We’re thrilled to welcome Kawhi back to Toronto. His impact on our organization, our city, and our country is undeniable, and he embodies the competitiveness and championship mindset that we value,” he said in the press release. “We believe his leadership, experience and talent will help us as we continue building toward our next championship. We also want to thank Brandon and Gradey and appreciate their work ethic, character, and basketball excellence they brought to our team every day.”
For Leonard, who averaged 27.9 points per game with his hometown team in California last season, the trade marks a reunion with the team he famously guided to the NBA championship in 2019. He will play under the guidance of Serbian play-caller Darko Rajakovic.

vistina: NBA Player Movement 2026-09-02: Cleveland Cavaliers signed center Khalifa Diop to a Contract.
tekst:
By Stefan Acevski / info@eurohoops.net
Khalifa Diop is now a Cleveland Cavaliers player. The Ohio franchise officially announced the signing of the former Baskonia center on Wednesday, September 2nd.
According to Marca, Baskonia canceled the friendly match against Gipuzkoa because they do not have enough players for it, and one of the reasons is Diop’s departure.
According to Michael Scotto, Khalifa Diop’s contract is for four years and $9.26 million. Only one year and $1.36 million are guaranteed.
The Senegalese center, chosen by the Cleveland Cavaliers with the 39th pick in the 2022 Draft, traveled with the club’s permission to Cleveland to undergo a medical examination.
The Cleveland Cavaliers released a statement regarding his signing:
The Cleveland Cavaliers have signed center Khalifa Diop (hah-LEE-fuh JYOP), Cavaliers President of Basketball Operations Koby Altman announced today from Cleveland Clinic Courts.
Diop (6-11, 231), who was selected by the Cavaliers with the 39th overall pick in the 2022 NBA Draft, has spent the past three seasons with Saski Baskonia of Spain’s Liga ACB and the EuroLeague. In 2025-26, the 24-year-old appeared in 47 total games (38 starts) for Baskonia and averaged 3.8 points on .670 shooting from the field, 4.2 rebounds and 0.7 blocks in 16.4 minutes per game. He helped Baskonia capture the 2026 Copa del Rey title, the club’s first in 17 years, after also contributing to the team’s 2023 EuroCup championship.
The Senegal native represented his country at the youth level, including the 2019 and 2021 FIBA U19 Basketball World Cups. Prior to being drafted in 2022, Diop earned 2021-22 EuroCup Rising Star honors while playing for Gran Canaria (Spain), an award presented to the best under-22 player in the EuroCup. He was also a member of the Cavaliers’ 2023 NBA Summer League championship team.
Diop will wear No. 18 for the Cavaliers.

vistina: NBA Player Movement 2026-08-20: LA Clippers received guard Max Strus from Cleveland Cavaliers.
tekst:
By Johnny Askounis/ info@eurohoops.net
Ismael Kamagate was included in the five-team trade, which was officially confirmed on Thursday.
As a component of this blockbuster transaction, the Los Angeles Clippers sent the draft rights of the 25-year-old French center to the Cleveland Cavaliers, as well as the second-round pick in 2027 to the Washington Wizards, to help facilitate the acquisition of 30-year-old Max Strus.
The Paris native has seen his NBA draft rights become a highly active trade asset since he was initially selected with the 46th overall pick in the 2022 NBA Draft, presented by State Farm. He has been moved sequentially from the Detroit Pistons to the Portland Trail Blazers, onward to the Denver Nuggets, then to the Clippers, and now finally lands with the Cavs.
On the international stage, Kamagate has represented France in the FIBA World Cup 2023 Qualifiers following his early development at the junior national level. His extensive European club career features nine Turkish Airlines EuroLeague games with EA7 Emporio Armani Milan, 41 7DAYS/BKT EuroCup games splitting time between Besiktas Gain and Paris, and 16 Basketball Champions League games with Bertram Derthona Tortona, amounting to a Star Lineup First Team nod. Heading into the 2026–27 season, he pinned a multiyear agreement with the BCL’s Openjobmetis Varese.
This finalized, multi-team agreement looping together the Clippers, Cavaliers, Wizards, Nuggets, and Charlotte Hornets seals a complex transaction highlighted by Cleveland landing Peyton Watson. The inclusion of Kamagate helps balance the asset distribution between all five participating franchises.
